title: SQL: tables that point at each other
summary: Why an order keeps a customer's number, not their name, and how JOIN puts rows back together.

text: A database splits data into tables, and each fact is written once.
- An order doesn't copy the customer's name: it keeps their id.
- Ada changes her name? One row to update, not every order.
JOIN … ON puts the matching rows side by side again. Ada shows twice: once for each of her orders.
The joined rows are a table like any other: you can filter them, add them up.
- GROUP BY customers.id gives one line per customer (two Adas stay apart).
